title: LA-RCS: LLM-agent-based Robot Control System

model.params_source: assumed (the paper states no decoding parameters for the baseline condition)

task.subset_rule: the 20 benchmark user requests of Sec. 4.1 (5 each for object detection, command execution, obstacle navigation, situational awareness); each request was run three times and the best run kept
task.approximation: The claim is the 'GPT-4 Turbo (Human Surrogate)' baseline: the model is asked for step-by-step guidance and a human operator executes the steps on the CAROBO robot. Only the guidance text can be produced by an API call; whether a request succeeded is decided by running the steps on the robot.

items.source: the 20 user requests are printed in Tables 2-5 (one table per domain); the project site https://la-rcs.github.io exists (HTTP 200) but publishes no dataset file

prompt.system: not printed: Sec. 3 says the LLM agent uses 'several shot-prompting methods' through a system message; Sec. 4.1 says the baselines were 'directed to provide step-by-step guidance'
prompt.user_template: not printed; the user message is one of the 20 benchmark requests, e.g. 'Move around and search for the location of the refrigerator'
prompt.few_shot: unstated ('several shot-prompting methods'; the examples are not printed)

output.postprocess: the reply is a list of steps for a human operator

metric.name: custom
metric.definition: success rate: the share of the 20 requests a human operator could complete by executing the model's steps on the robot; a request counts as failed when the model declares completion without the task being done or loops on meaningless movements (Sec. 4.1)
metric.judge: human operator plus the physical CAROBO robot
metric.original_location: Table 1, row 'GPT-4 Turbo (Human Surrogate)', column Success rate (%) (average step count 9.5)

open_points: No prompt text is printed: only the framing (system message, few-shot) is described, and the number and content of the shots are unknown.
The metric cannot be computed from model output: success is decided by a human operator executing the steps on a physical robot in the authors' environment.
Best-of-three scoring: each request was run three times and the best run kept, which is not one of the harness's aggregation rules.
notes: The full agentic condition 'LA-RCS (GPT-4 Turbo)' (60% success, Table 1) needs the robot interface as well, so it is no more reproducible than the surrogate baseline. Fig. 3 gives the per-domain rates and Tables 2-5 the per-request outcomes.
